original.target_description: Second randomized condition: incorrect matching of image A to Obama and image B to Trump, compared across Trump voters, Clinton voters and nonvoters; Figure 4, discussed on journal p. 141 (PDF p. 7). This is identification of the president/inauguration, not choosing which photograph has more people.

notes: Original-only blind validation. Published 2018 article, DOI/title/authors verified in supplied primary text. PDF target pages visually inspected; printed journal pages 139–141 correspond to PDF pages 5–7. Canonical text agrees with rendered numeric values; original line-break hyphenation is retained in quotes. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Requested OR, test statistic, and p for this vote-choice comparison are not printed. Narrative reports approximately 40 percent of Trump voters, about 20 percent of nonvoters, and less than 10 percent of Clinton voters misidentified the pictures; no odds ratio or p was derived. Figure 2 first-condition group Ns do not establish second-condition analytic Ns. The p = .025 earlier on p. 141 belongs to the first-condition education comparison among strong approvers and was not reused. The paper describes vote choice rather than Republican/Democrat identification. Figure 4 and its caption on journal p. 142 were inspected in supplied canonical text; target discussion on p. 141 was visually checked in the rendered PDF.
